saints.name: St. Vitus
saints.title: Martyr
saints.shortBlurb: A boy martyr of the early Church, one of the Fourteen Holy Helpers invoked in sickness…
biography: According to his ancient acts, Vitus was the young son of a pagan senator in Sicily who was converted as a child by his tutor Modestus and his nurse Crescentia. Fleeing his father's anger, the three were seized in the persecution of Diocletian and put to death about the year 303.

His veneration spread widely through the West, and he came to be numbered among the Fourteen Holy Helpers. He is invoked against epilepsy and the nervous disorder long called “St. Vitus's Dance,” and is honored as a patron of dancers and actors.
saints.knownFor: One of the Fourteen Holy Helpers; patron of dancers.

sources.text: The Roman Martyrology (1914 English ed.; public domain)
